sections.label: Employment Claims Tribunals proposed
sections.summary: The proposed Employment Claims Tribunals will help more employees resolve more types of salary-related disputes with employers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: To ensure that our employment dispute resolution landscape remains relevant going forward, the proposed Employment Claims Tribunals (ECT) will help more employees resolve more types of salary-related disputes with their employers.

sections.label: ECT hears contractual salary claims
sections.summary: The ECT will hear contractual salary-related claims from more employees, including PMEs earning more than $4,500 per month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Besides hearing statutory salary-related claims from employees covered under the EA, RRA and CDCA, the ECT will also hear contractual salary-related claims from more employees, including PMEs who earn more than $4,500 per month and are currently beyond the coverage of the EA.

sections.label: Labour Court mediation resolution
sections.summary: More than 90% of Labour Court claims will be resolved at mediation without formal hearings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: More than 90% of Labour Court claims will be resolved at the mediation stage without having to go through formal hearings.

sections.label: Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management
sections.summary: Tripartite Partners will set up a new centre known as the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Tripartite Partners will set up a new centre known as the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM).

sections.label: Excluded executives and expanded disputes
sections.summary: Only executive employees with substantial managerial responsibilities will continue to be excluded, and TMF dispute types will be expanded.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Only executive employees with substantial managerial responsibilities will continue to be excluded due to a potential conflict of interest.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: The types of disputes covered under the TMF will be 	Page: 80 expanded to include re-employment and other statutory employment benefits, for example, overtime pay, public holiday pay and maternity benefits under the EA and CDCA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: First, the claims limit will be $30,000 per case for cases which go through mediation with union involvement, compared to $20,000 for all other claims.

sections.label: ECT and TADM establishment date
sections.summary: With the passing of the Bill today, the ECT and TADM will be established by April 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: With the passing of the Bill today, the ECT and TADM will be established by April 2017.

sections.label: ECT plugs EA salary cap gap
sections.summary: The speaker applauds the ECT for plugging the EA's gap, which has a $4,500 salary cap for PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I applaud the setting up of the ECT for five reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: It plugs the existing gap of the EA, which has a $4,500 salary cap for PMEs.

sections.label: ECT jurisdiction over employment claims
sections.summary: The ECT will have jurisdiction over 18 contractual and 43 statutory employment claims available to all workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The ECT will have jurisdiction over 18 types of contractual employment claims and 43 types of statutory 	Page: 81 employment claims which are availed to all workers.

sections.label: TMF expansion for union members
sections.summary: For union members, TMF will be expanded with no salary limits, covering four existing claims over and above the 18 and 43 items.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In fact, for union members, besides representation by unions, as shared by the Minister earlier, TMF will also be similarly expanded with no salary limits and cover the four existing types of TMF claims over and above the 18 contractual and 43 statutory items where applicable.

sections.label: Review IRA to expand TMF
sections.summary: The speaker submits MOM should support another IRA review to expand TMF to areas not covered by the ECT, such as unfair dismissal outside the EA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am aware our Tripartite Mediation covers an additional four areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: But I submit that MOM should support another review of the IRA to further expand the TMF to extend to areas beyond the 18/43 and the existing four areas to cover those areas not covered by the ECT, such as unfair dismissal of workers outside of the ambit of the EA.

sections.label: Agreement enforceable via District Court
sections.summary: The agreement will also be enforceable if registered in a District Court via section 7(3).

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The agreement will also be enforceable if it is registered in a District Court via section 7(3).

sections.label: Mediation should not delay claims
sections.summary: Mediation before the ECT hearing should never delay aggrieved workers' claims if a summary or expedited hearing can be convened without mediation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: While the introduction of mediation before the ECT hearing is convened is a positive move, it should never prevent the aggrieved workers from having their claim delayed and their livelihood and work severely affected if the case can be summarily heard or an expedited hearing can be convened without the need for mediation.

sections.label: ECT claims limits and coverage
sections.summary: Speaker suggests regular review of claims limits and urges MOM to ensure the ECT is practical, effective, encompassing, accessible and enforceable for all workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: To stay effective and relevant, I further suggest that the claims limits be regularly reviewed and adjusted to stay relevant, inclusive and appropriate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In setting up the ECT, I urge MOM to look into five important aspects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: It must be practical, effective, encompassing, accessible and enforceable, so that it not only benefits white-collar and blue-collar workers, but also protects freelancers, apprentices and interns.

sections.label: ECT employee coverage and exceptions
sections.summary: The ECT will cover all employees with an employment contract regardless of salary, except public servants, domestic workers and seafarers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The ECT will basically cover all employees who have an employment contract with the employers regardless of their salary level, with the exception of the following three groups of employees: one, public servants; two, domestic workers; and three, seafarers.

sections.label: Pregnant mothers' unfair dismissal cases
sections.summary: In 2013, Tan Chuan-Jin said MOM received an average of 70 cases annually from female employees from 2007 to 2013, 70% pregnant mothers alleging unfair dismissal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2013, for instance, the then Acting Minister for Manpower, Mr Tan Chuan-Jin, said that from between the period 2007 and 2013, MOM received an average of 70 cases from female employees annually, 70% of whom are pregnant mothers who felt that they had been unfairly dismissed.

sections.label: Fees for Labour Court documents
sections.summary: Claimants presently pay $5 per page for notes of evidence and grounds of decision by the Labour Court Commissioner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Presently, claimants have to pay $5 per page for the notes of evidence and grounds of decision made by the Labour Court Commissioner.

sections.label: Proposed ECT fee caps and waivers
sections.summary: Speaker proposes fees be pegged at no higher than $160 for salary-related claims, as in the UK, and waived entirely for those in financial distress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Considering that our claimants could be facing financial difficulties and are seeking recourse through the ECT, I would like to propose that the fees be pegged at no higher than $160 for salary-related claims, a practice common in the UK, and it should be waived entirely for those in financial distress.

sections.label: ECT to hear salary and CPF claims
sections.summary: Speaker urges the Ministry to let the ECT look into both salary and CPF claims to make filing salary-related grievances easier for workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: First, I would like to urge the Ministry to allow the ECT to look into both salary and Central Provident Fund (CPF) claims to make it easier for workers to file salary claims related grievances.

sections.label: First mediation session timing
sections.summary: Proposes that the first mediation session be held at least 14 days after referral to the approved mediator.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Third, I would like to propose that the first mediation session be held at least 14 days after it is referred to the approved mediator.

sections.label: Administrative fees for low-wage workers
sections.summary: Proposes waiving administrative fees for valid cases involving low-wage workers already affected by non-payment of salaries when they file claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Fifth, I would also like to propose that administrative fees be waived for valid cases involving low-wage workers who are already affected by non-payment of salaries when they file claims.

sections.label: Bill timing and union representation
sections.summary: States the current Bill is timely for several reasons and urges that unions be allowed to represent their members in the claims process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   The current Bill is timely for several reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I also strongly urge that unions be allowed to represent their respective members in the claims process.

sections.label: ECT representation and ministerial exemption
sections.summary: Quotes section 5(1)c barring agent representation in ECT mediation and section 34(1)(d) allowing the Minister to exempt persons by regulations.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Section 5(1)c states that a claimant "cannot be represented by an agent, whether paid or otherwise" in the ECT mediation process; and section 34(1)(d) states that "the Minister may make regulations to exempt any person or class of persons from all or any of the provisions of this Act, either generally or in a particular case".

sections.label: Claim limits, splitting and abandonment
sections.summary: Describes section 12(7) claim limits, section 14 bar on dividing claims, and section 15 option to abandon excess claim amounts.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to section 12(7), there are set limits on the claims, but the exact amount is silent in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Section 14 states that "a claim cannot be divided and pursued in separate proceedings before a tribunal if the only reason for doing so is to bring the total amount alleged to be payable in each of those proceedings within the jurisdiction of a tribunal", while section 15 gives claimants the option to abandon the part of the claim that exceeds the set limit so that they can be eligible for hearing at the tribunal.

sections.label: Contempt under Administration of Justice Bill
sections.summary: States that under the Administration of Justice Bill passed last night, this would be an act of contempt of Court.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Under the Administration of Justice Bill, which was passed last night, this would be an act of contempt of Court.

sections.label: Non-monetary claims in ECT
sections.summary: Asks whether non-monetary claims like unfair dismissal and discrimination could be included in the ECT or if current alternative avenues suffice.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can non-monetary claims, such as unfair dismissal, discrimination, be included within the ambit of the ECT in future or are the alternative avenues at present sufficient?

sections.label: ECT coverage and claim caps
sections.summary: States the ECT covers workers not under the EA, especially PMEs earning over $4,500 monthly, with claims capped at $20,000 or $30,000.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: First, the most important feature of the ECT is that it covers workers not covered under the EA, especially PMEs who earn more than $4,500 a month.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, the obstacles faced by PMEs might return in another form with the tribunal.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It was stated in the MOM's public consultation exercise that claims amount would be capped at $20,000 per claim, or $30,000, if claimants go through the TMF or MOM conciliation.

sections.label: Salary dispute clearance figures
sections.summary: The Minister said 1,630 salary dispute cases were cleared in 2014, with one-third not fully paid and 80% of those employers able to pay.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Minister for Manpower said in his reply to a Parliamentary Question in May 2015 that the Ministry cleared 1,630 cases of salary disputes in 2014, but one-third of workers did not receive the full payment on the pretext that the companies which owed them salaries were facing financial difficulties.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: When the Ministry investigated further, 80% of the employers who did not make full payment were discovered to be able to make the full payment.

sections.label: Public concerns on Bill
sections.summary: Asks the Minister to inform the House of key public concerns on the Bill and responses, and to publish the summary online.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would the Minister inform the House what are some of the key concerns the public had with the Bill and the Ministry's responses to them?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would the Minister also please cause the summary of responses to be published online?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Since 2008, PMETs have made up a majority of the resident workforce.

sections.label: MOM programmes for PMETs
sections.summary: States MOM delved into underlying problems with initiatives including Professional Conversion Programmes from 2007 and the Career Support Programme in October 2015.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MOM, in particular, has not held back and instead, delved deep into the underlying problems with initiatives, such as the Professional Conversion Programmes beginning in 2007 and the Career Support Programme in October 2015, as well.

sections.label: Reason for $30,000 cap
sections.summary: Asks the reason for setting the maximum claims at $30,000, even allowing for mediation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What is the reason for setting the maximum claims at $30,000, even allowing for mediation?

sections.label: Guidelines for tribunal decisions
sections.summary: A framework for tribunal guidelines would clarify whether it must consider unemployment periods and the economy's direction in setting awards.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A framework for stipulating guidelines for the tribunal's decisions and awards would clarify the approach that the tribunal should take, in particular, whether it has to take into account the consequences of periods of higher unemployment, as well as whether it should consider the direction of the economy in setting awards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Page: 92 My first concern is on representations in proceedings in clause 19(2)(e).

sections.label: Enforcement of tribunal orders
sections.summary: The speaker suggests stronger enforcement rules: criminalising default, personal liability for directors, escrow funds, and a worker fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As such, I would suggest stronger rules be put in place for the enforcement of tribunal orders and settlements: (a) making it a criminal offence to default on these orders; (b) if directors wind up companies and set up new ones, claimants should be allowed to return to the ECT to make directors, major shareholders and officers personally liable to fulfil the orders; (c) the ECT should hold the funds in escrow to be disbursed to the claimants as employers are less likely to default on payments to be made directly to the Court; and lastly, (d) for bankrupted companies experiencing genuine financial difficulties, a fund could be created to help workers, financed by corporate tax or the security bond paid by employers.

sections.label: Cost of Labour Court records
sections.summary: Claimants pay $5 per page for Labour Court records, with one charity documenting a case costing almost $1,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the current Labour Court system, claimants have to pay $5 per page for these records.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One charity has documented a case where a claimant had to pay almost $1,000 – a large sum for low-wage workers.

sections.label: Unfair dismissal cases statistics
sections.summary: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin said MOM received an average of 70 female unfair dismissal cases yearly from 2007 to 2012, 70% involving pregnant women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In January 2013, the then Acting Minister for Manpower, Mr Tan Chuan-Jin, said that from 2007 to 2012, MOM received annually an average of 70 cases from female employees who felt that they have been unfairly dismissed, out of which, 70% involved pregnant women.

sections.label: Proposed time bar length
sections.summary: The proposed time bar of one year and six months is extremely short compared to the six-year limit in State and High Courts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Comparing the statutory time limit for claims in the State and High Courts for employment contracts-related claims which is six years, the proposed time bar of one year and six months respectively is extremely short.

sections.label: Claim limits under Bill
sections.summary: Under this Bill, claims are limited to $20,000 or $30,000 for claimants going through TMF or MOM conciliation under the IRA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under this Bill, claims are limited to $20,000 or $30,000 for claimants to go through the TMF or MOM conciliation prescribed under the IRA.

sections.label: High Court variation prohibition
sections.summary: Clause 25(2) prohibits the High Court from varying the tribunal's decision on a question of fact or receiving further evidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The High Court is prohibited by clause 25(2) of this Bill to vary the tribunal's decision on the question of fact or to receive further evidence.

sections.label: ECT for PMET conflicts
sections.summary: Setting up the ECT to settle conflicts between PMETs and employers is described as a good move.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Setting up the ECT to settle conflicts between PMETs and employers is a good move.

sections.label: Employers' knowledge after Bill
sections.summary: After the Bill is passed, employers have to step up on their knowledge in this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: After this Bill has been passed, employers have to step up on their knowledge in this.

sections.label: SMEs' tribunal preparation burden
sections.summary: Preparing documents and following detailed procedures in the tribunal would be extremely exacting for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Whenever conflicts arise and need to be raised in the tribunal, just the preparation of documents, and following up on detailed procedures, would be extremely exacting for SMEs.

sections.label: Employment Claims Bill and ECT
sections.summary: The Bill establishes an ECT in the State Courts, replacing the Labour Court and extending jurisdiction to employees not covered by the EA, such as PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How does one then differentiate between standard HR adjustments and unreasonable salary conflicts?

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Employment Claims Bill seeks to establish an ECT within the State Courts to facilitate the expeditious resolution of certain specified employment disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In addition, the Tribunal will replace the Labour Court, which is a dispute resolution mechanism currently administered by the Commissioner for Labour to adjudicate on employment claims by employees who are covered by the EA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In contrast, the tribunal's jurisdiction will extend to adjudicating on employment claims of employees not covered by the EA, such as PMEs.

sections.label: Representatives and tribunal limits
sections.summary: The tribunal will be limited to employment disputes of up to S$20,000 normally or $30,000 for claimants invoking IRA mediation or conciliation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Does he contemplate that these representatives would be legally trained and, if so, how would that reconcile with the principle of section 19 of the Bill?

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I understand that the tribunal will be limited to hearing employment disputes of up to S$20,000 for normal cases or $30,000 for claimants invoking mediation or conciliation under the IRA.

sections.label: Salary dispute regulations and Commissioner
sections.summary: Section 38(e) amends the EA so the Commissioner must not decide salary-related disputes unless prescribed by regulations, and the tribunal is expected to take over such claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In particular, in relation to the salary-related disputes under the EA, section 38(e) of the Bill will make consequential amendments to section 115 of the EA, to provide that the Commissioner must not inquire into or decide a salary-related dispute unless the dispute is of a type prescribed by regulations made under section 139 of the EA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Having regard to that fact, the tribunal is expected to take over the work of the Commissioner for Labour in adjudicating salary-related claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Could the Minister please clarify what kind of regulations under the EA are contemplated and in what situations would it be permissible for an employee to make a claim to the Commissioner under the EA?

sections.label: Section 16(7) and mediation
sections.summary: Section 16(7) of the Bill appears antithetical to the purpose of mediation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, section 16(7) of the Bill appears antithetical to the purpose of mediation.

sections.label: Unfair workplace practice complaints
sections.summary: TAFEP received 259 unfair practice complaints in 2014 versus 475 in 2013, mostly on hiring disadvantaging Singaporeans by age, language and race, with little data on unreported cases.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: According to the TAFEP, 259 complaints were received about unfair practices at the workplace in 2014, compared to 475 made in 2013.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: While there is a trend of decline in the complaints, most of the complaints received were related to hiring practices which disadvantaged Singaporeans and they were based on age, language and race.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: However, there has been little survey statistics available about the percentage of unfair dismissal of workers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Similarly, not much attention has been given to unfair practices that go unreported by the workers who were so affected who may not be covered by the Act or due to lack of knowledge on their entitlements or for fear of losing their jobs, especially when the job market is weak.

sections.label: Resident earning $1,900 monthly
sections.summary: A resident earns a monthly salary of $1,900 and has worked for a local SME for the past 18 years.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: The second case is that of a resident whose monthly salary is $1,900 and works for a local SME for the past 18 years.

sections.label: Claims process and waiting period
sections.summary: He stayed in his job and would pursue overdue claims only if he secures external work, as claims and appeals may take six months to a year, a taxing wait for workers with special circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: He thus remained in his job and decided to pursue all overdue claims if he is able to, only provided that he can secure a job externally and because he has got four members in his family to care for.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: So, having a claims process and tribunal may be a start for those seeking help, but the claims and appeal cases to be heard could easily take between six months and up to a year.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: This is a very arduous waiting period and is mentally and physically taxing for many of these workers, especially those who have special circumstances, like those who are sole breadwinners, have unexpected health conditions and or are actually silent individuals who do not dare to contest for their job rights or make the next "big" move into the next job.

sections.label: Multi-pronged approaches to discrimination
sections.summary: Resolving these issues requires multi-pronged approaches beyond basic age, race or language discrimination, including stepped-up audits, external valuations, stemming weak sector practices and continued education.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: In order to resolve them, it requires multi-pronged approaches to strike a balance or to mitigate their effects, and many of these effects go beyond the basics of what are considered discrimination on grounds of age, race or even language at the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: I encourage the agencies to consider stepping up on audits, doing external valuations to benchmark, identifying and stemming the current weak practices in some of the sectors, while the educational aspect continues to be communicated and implemented.

sections.label: Excluded workers and claim ceiling
sections.summary: Civil servants, domestic workers and seafarers are excluded for now; the speaker suggests pegging the claim ceiling to inflation and regrets other disputes cannot be heard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For now, civil servants, domestic workers and seafarers will be excluded as they have other avenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In addition, may I suggest that the ceiling for claims be pegged to our inflation rate so that it will be revised periodically in a timely manner?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am disappointed that other workplace disputes, such as emotional and physical abuse, discrimination and unfair dismissal, cannot be resolved through this tribunal.

sections.label: Court provisions and abandoned excess
sections.summary: The speaker asks what provisions the Court has, noting clause 15 lets a claimant abandon the excess so the tribunal has jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would the Minister share with the House what provisions does the Court have in such situations?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I note that under clause 15, the claimant may abandon the excess amount, so that the tribunal has jurisdiction to hear and determine the claim.

sections.label: Recourse through ECT
sections.summary: They would have recourse through the ECT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Yes, they would have recourse through the ECT.

sections.label: Non-payment of CPF offence
sections.summary: Non-payment of CPF contribution is an offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, non-payment of CPF contribution is an offence.

sections.label: ECT takes over Labour Court
sections.summary: The ECT will take over the role of the Labour Court and not beyond that, with these worker categories considered for future phases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The ECT, for a good start, will take over the role of the Labour Court and not beyond that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Therefore, for these categories of workers, we will look to include them in future phases of implementation.

sections.label: First Labour Court session timing
sections.summary: For Labour Court claims, the first session is arranged within a month, usually within 14 working days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: For Labour Court claims, the first session is arranged within a month, usually within 14 working days.

sections.label: No legal representation at ECT
sections.summary: The reason for insisting on no legal representation at the ECT is that it would disadvantage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The reason why we insist on no legal representation at the ECT is because we think legal representation will work to 	Page: 104 the disadvantage of the workers.

sections.label: Union representation at ECT
sections.summary: Union members in unionised companies may be represented by their unions at mediation and ECT hearings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Several Members also asked about the representation at the ECT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: I just want to confirm again that for union members in the unionised companies, they may be represented by the unions at mediation and at the ECT hearings.

sections.label: ECT fees and low-wage workers
sections.summary: The ECT will be accessible to low-wage workers and fees will be waived for deserving cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Mr Faisal Manap was concerned that the fees may be set too high and he 	Page: 105 hoped that it would be set below $160 or something like that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: I would also like to assure Mr Zainal Sapari and Mr Faisal Manap that the ECT will be accessible to low-wage workers and we will waive the fees for deserving cases, which is in line with today's State Courts' practice.

sections.label: Employers paying Labour Court orders
sections.summary: Of all employers who receive Labour Court orders, 80% were able to pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: What I meant was that of all the employers who receive Labour Court orders, 80% were able to pay.

sections.label: Commissioner for Labour continues claims
sections.summary: The Commissioner for Labour will continue to hear transfer of employment, salary recovery and non-salary-related disputes such as unfair dismissal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: With the setting up of the ECT, the Commissioner for Labour will continue to hear claims related to the transfer of employment to another company because of restructuring, and claims related to the recovery of salary not paid in legal tender.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In addition, the Commissioner for Labour will continue to handle non-salary-related disputes, such as unfair dismissal.

sections.label: ECT rules on EAP adequacy
sections.summary: If parties cannot agree on the Employment Assistance Payment, the ECT will rule whether it is adequate and appropriate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Once it is determined that the employee is eligible for re-employment, if they cannot agree on the payment of the Employment Assistance Payment (EAP), that is where the ECT will come in to rule whether the payment is adequate and appropriate.

sections.label: ECT salary dispute scope
sections.summary: Tripartite partners agreed the ECT should first resolve salary-related dispute claims affordably and expeditiously before considering non salary-related issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The tripartite partners have deliberated at length and we have decided and agreed that the ECT should start with resolving salary-related dispute claims in an affordable and expeditious manner now, before we consider to expand the scope of the ECT to hear non salary-related issues in future.

sections.label: EAP eligibility re-employment check
sections.summary: For EAP payment cases, eligibility for re-employment is established first, since payment does not arise if the employee is ineligible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: My understanding is that, if a case is relating to the payment of the EAP, the first to be established is whether the employee is eligible for re-employment because, if the employee is not eligible for re-employment, then the payment of the EAP does not arise.

sections.label: MOM decides re-employment eligibility
sections.summary: An employee who disagrees with the mediator on eligibility can go to MOM, which is the final decision-maker on re-employment eligibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: If the employee disagrees with the mediator that he does not qualify for eligibility, he can come to MOM, and MOM is the final decision-maker to decide whether a worker is eligible for re-employment.

sections.label: Labour Court order payment rates
sections.summary: Of all employers who received a Labour Court order for payment, 80% made payment and only 20% did not pay in full.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Basically, what I meant to say was that of all the companies, of all the employers who received the Labour Court order for payment, 80% actually were able to make payment; only 20% did not make the full payment.

sections.label: ECT order enforceable via District Court
sections.summary: For those not covered under the EA, the ECT order is enforceable by registering the settlement outcome with the District Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: For those not covered under the EA, the advantage of the ECT is that the order of the ECT is now enforceable by registering the settlement outcome with the District Court.
